correctness.rationale: The proof gives an exact character-by-character identity for all n≥3: diagonal colour translation annihilates unbalanced frequencies; closed nonzero edge increments and the orthogonality filter reduce the balanced sum to three integer powers (-2)^{c_r}; their only possible zero is the histogram (a,a,a+1); multinomial counting gives Z_n and diagonalization gives rank. The boundary n=3 and the b_n=0 normalization were checked. Two independently structured exact-integer implementations check every character for n=3,...,7; scripts form part of this package. The asymptotic follows by the stated Stirling formula. No finite computation is substituted for an infinite proof.

evidence: Sokal, arXiv:math/0503607v1, §§2.2 and 2.4: classical chromatic counts and a general abelian Fourier duality. The cycle formula concerns unweighted colour counts.

Ellis-Monaghan–Moffatt, arXiv:1005.5470v2, Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.3: a general vertex-weighted Potts polynomial and spanning-subgraph expression for arbitrary local fields, not the closed ternary cycle Fourier cancellation histogram.

Babson–Beck, arXiv:1204.1283v1, pages 1–4: an abelian Fourier derivation for probabilities of graph colourings and a reciprocity law indexed by bridgeless spanning subgraphs, not all site Fourier multipliers.
Shrock–Xu, arXiv:1009.1182v1, §X: set-weighted cycle partition functions with a uniform field affecting a subset of colours, not arbitrary vertex-dependent root-of-unity fields.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general V-polynomial can evaluate arbitrary locally weighted colour sums and thus provides an algorithmic expression for the coefficients as a special instance. It does not itself supply the explicit three-power reduction, complete exact zero locus, multinomial multiplicities, or all-order rank; deriving these is the substantive claim. The cycle count and Fourier flow duality likewise do not settle the multiplier-zero question.

value.rationale: The claim identifies a sharp mod-three transition in injectivity of a natural counting convolution on the colour-translation quotient, for an infinite family of cyclic graphs. It gives the complete spectrum and exact dimension of information loss at every order (with an asymptotic rarity law). This is a motivated structural boundary at the first nontrivial cyclic block beyond trees, not simply the classical number of colourings or a finite table.
